extracted.intended_audience: working adults and professionals interested in improving work–life balance (TED audience/general public)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for structuring an "ideal day" that balances family time, personal time, and productive work, and for taking personal responsibility to implement that balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal day balanced between family time, personal time and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Marsh lays out an ideal day balanced between family time, personal time and productivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an explicit daily schedule or "ideal day" as a template to allocate time across three domains (family, personal, work/productivity). Treat the ideal-day model as a concrete planning tool for everyday decisions about time use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal responsibility for work–life balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Work-life balance, says Nigel Marsh, is too important to be left in the hands of your employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on employers or external structures to create balance; actively make choices and set boundaries to shape your own work–life arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take action to make balance happen
rubrics_metrics.description: Marsh offers encouragement to make it happen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move from recognition to implementation: be proactive about making changes (even small ones) to align daily life with the ideal-day vision rather than passively wishing for balance.
